title: After Trent: is habitual grace of faith? Soto denies
source_text: XIX. Et quanquam hodie nullus est post Concilium Tridentinum, qui Pighium sequatur; & sententia ejus communiter damnetur, saltem ut valde temeraria: nihilominus adhuc inter se disputant Scholae Romanae Theologi An de fide sit dari gratiam habitualem, & an Concilia praedicta intenderint rem illam, tanquam de fide definire. Quod post Concilium Tridentinum, negavit Dominicus Soto Doctor insignis, qui illi interfuit. Licet communiter alii sentiant probabilius esse quod dogma istud sit de fide.
pass_a_gloss: XIX. And although today there is no one after the Council of Trent, who follows Pighius; and his opinion is commonly condemned, at least as very rash: nevertheless still the Theologians of the Roman School dispute among themselves Whether it is of faith that habitual grace is given, and whether the said Councils intended to define that thing, as of faith. Which after the Council of Trent, Dominic Soto a notable Doctor, who was present at it, denied. Although commonly others think it more probable that this dogma is of faith.
pass_b_english: Thesis XIX. Since the Council of Trent nobody follows Pighius, and his view is commonly condemned, at the least as very rash. Even so, the theologians of the Roman School still argue among themselves whether it is a matter of faith that habitual grace is given, and whether those councils meant to define the point as of faith.
After the Council of Trent, Domingo de Soto, a distinguished doctor who had been present at it, denied that they did. Others commonly hold it more probable that this teaching is of faith.

lemmas.latin: An de fide sit dari gratiam habitualem
lemmas.gloss: Whether it is of faith that habitual grace is given

lemmas.latin: negavit Dominicus Soto Doctor insignis, qui illi interfuit
lemmas.gloss: Dominic Soto a notable Doctor, who was present at it, denied

choices.why: A doctrine defined so that denying it is heresy; Soto denied Trent had raised habitual grace to that level.
